question: Write an email that responds to the situation above. You have 7 minutes.
answer:
Dear Ms. Okafor,

Thank you for organizing the volunteer day at the community garden last Saturday. I really enjoyed it, and I met many friendly people.

In the morning, I helped two other students plant tomatoes and beans near the fence. After lunch, I watered the flower beds and carried bags of soil to the shed. It was hard work, but I felt very happy when I saw the finished garden.

I have one small suggestion. Some volunteers did not know where the tools were, so we lost time looking for them. Next time, you could put a simple map or a sign on the shed door. I think this would really help new volunteers.

I hope I can help again next month.

Best regards,
Daniel

Dear Dr. Lindqvist,

I am writing on behalf of the volunteers who run the campus bike repair workshop. We were disappointed to learn that the workshop will close next semester to make room for additional staff parking.

Our concern is that this decision works against the university's own climate plan, which aims to cut commuting emissions by a quarter. Last year alone, the workshop repaired more than six hundred bicycles at little or no cost, and many students told us they would have started driving if they had not been able to fix their bikes cheaply.

We understand that parking is limited. However, we wonder whether a compromise is possible. The workshop could move to the unused storage room beside the sports center, which we would be happy to clean and prepare ourselves.

I would welcome the chance to discuss this with you.

Respectfully,
Aisha Bello

Elena Vasquez

Hana

Oliver Grant

Thomas Nguyen

passage:
You work as a research assistant on a health study. Today you discovered that a spreadsheet containing participants' names and medical information has been saved in a folder that all lab members can access.

Write an email to your supervisor, Dr. Carvalho. In your email, do the following:
- Describe what you found.
- Explain why this is a problem.
- Suggest steps that should be taken.

Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
question: Write an email that responds to the situation above. You have 7 minutes.
answer:
Dear Dr. Carvalho,

I am writing about a data security issue I found this morning. While looking for the interview schedule, I found a spreadsheet in the shared lab folder that contains the full names, birth dates, and medical histories of around eighty participants in our study.

This is a serious concern because our ethics approval states that identifiable data must be stored only on the encrypted server, with access limited to the three named researchers. At present, more than twenty people, including visiting students, can open the shared folder, which means participants' confidentiality may already have been compromised.

I would suggest that we move the file to the secure server immediately and check the folder's access log to see who has opened it. It may also be necessary to report the incident to the ethics committee.

Best regards,
Daniela Ruiz

question: Write an email that responds to the situation above. You have 7 minutes.
answer:
Dear Ms. Ortega,

My professor has advised me to contact your office about ethics approval for a class project.

My project will examine the relationship between students' sleep habits and their part-time work. I plan to send an anonymous online survey to about one hundred undergraduate students. The survey will ask how many hours they usually sleep and how many hours they work each week. I will not collect names or any personal contact information.

Could you please tell me which forms I need to submit? I would also like to know whether a short, anonymous survey like mine requires a full review or whether there is a simpler process.

Finally, how long does the approval process usually take? My project is due at the end of next month, so I would like to begin collecting data as soon as possible.

Thank you for your help.

Sincerely,
Ahmed Karimi
